title: Mermaid Planning And Data Diagrams Questionnaire
concept: Choosing, writing, and reviewing planning and data-oriented Mermaid diagrams

questions.prompt: Which question is a Gantt diagram best equipped to answer?

options.label: When do tasks occur, how long do they take, and which tasks depend on others?
How many orders may belong to one customer?
Which API participant sends the third runtime message?

questions.explanation: Correct: Gantt encodes dates, durations, task status, and dependencies. Incorrect options: record cardinality belongs in an ER diagram; participant message order belongs in a sequence diagram.

questions.prompt: What does `Review :review, after examples, 2d` mean in a Mermaid Gantt task?

options.label: The review task starts after the task whose ID is examples and lasts two days.
The review starts two hours before examples.
The line creates a new section named examples.

questions.explanation: Correct: `after examples` is a task dependency and `2d` is duration. Incorrect options: `2d` means days and the direction is after, not before; sections require the `section` keyword.

questions.prompt: Which line correctly defines a user-journey task with score 5 and two participating actors?

options.label: See diagram render: 5: Learner, Renderer
Learner -->|5| Renderer
See diagram render :done, 5d

questions.explanation: Correct: journey tasks use `Task: score: actor list`. Incorrect options: the arrow is flowchart syntax and does not encode a journey score; `:done, 5d` is Gantt task metadata.

questions.prompt: Which dataset is the best fit for a pie chart?

options.label: Four mutually exclusive categories that together make up all review findings.
Request latency measured every minute for a week.
Monthly gains and losses containing positive and negative values.

questions.explanation: Correct: a few categories forming one whole suit part-to-whole comparison. Incorrect options: a time series needs an axis-based chart; negative values do not form meaningful pie-slice proportions.

questions.prompt: What determines parent-child hierarchy in a Mermaid mindmap?

options.label: Indentation beneath the parent node
Explicit `-->` arrows between every item
Chronological dates before every item

questions.explanation: Correct: mindmaps are indentation-sensitive and nesting defines hierarchy. Incorrect options: explicit arrows belong to flow-like grammars; dated events belong to timeline or Gantt diagrams.

questions.prompt: Why choose a timeline instead of a Gantt chart for a short history of architecture decisions?

options.label: The explanation needs ordered events but not task durations or dependency scheduling.
Timeline automatically validates database foreign keys.
Timeline shows request messages along participant lifelines.

questions.explanation: Correct: timeline emphasizes chronology without schedule mechanics. Incorrect options: no Mermaid timeline validates database constraints; lifelines and runtime messages are sequence-diagram concepts.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest use for a hand-authored Mermaid Git graph?

options.label: Explain a focused branching and merge strategy with only the relevant commits.
Replace the repository as the authoritative record of every commit hash.
Document database table cardinality.

questions.explanation: Correct: Git graph is effective for a simplified branch-and-merge story. Incorrect options: Git itself remains the source of exact history; database cardinality belongs in an ER diagram.

questions.prompt: A newer diagram family works in the Mermaid Live Editor but fails in the app. What should the author check first?

options.label: The Mermaid version and configuration actually deployed by the app
Whether adding more nodes makes the parser discover the grammar
Whether the Markdown file can be renamed to an image extension

questions.explanation: Correct: syntax support belongs to the host's installed Mermaid version and configuration. Incorrect options: extra nodes cannot add parser support; renaming source does not turn text into a rendered image or solve compatibility.
